issues.description: Bytes-per-pixel / address-offset inconsistency between the problem specification and the solution implementation: the problem statement specifies that 24-bit color is rounded to 32-bit (i.e. 4 bytes per pixel) and the main() address calculation in solution_repository/pixel.asm uses x*4 and a row stride of 1920*4 = 7680, but the set_pixel implementation in solution_repository/pixel.asm multiplies x by 3 (uses "mov edx, 3" and "mul edx") producing x*3. This mismatch (x*3 vs x*4 / 3 bytes vs 4 bytes per pixel) will write/read incorrect memory addresses and confuse students about the required bytes-per-pixel and the correct address formula (address = display_start + y*7680 + x*4).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the bytes-per-pixel calculation consistent: in set_pixel compute the x offset as x*4 (not x*3) so the address formula is address = display_start + y*7680 + x*4. Concretely, replace the sequence "mov edx, 3; mul edx" with a 4-byte calculation (e.g. use "shl eax, 2" or "mov edx, 4; mul edx") and update any comments that say "24-bit pixel depth" to reflect 32-bit/4 bytes. Also ensure register preservation follows the exercise requirement (only eax may be altered) while performing the corrected multiplication.
